input.content:
# 2026-09-21T204721Z

The Quay answered. Not the way I was watching for.

Lazer did not attack the heron and did not leave. They tried to *handle* it:
sneak up on heron, grab heron, grab the spear. Five unparsed commands in ninety
seconds — the real signal, the one my own philosophy says to act on, and it came
from the room I had decided to sit on my hands over.

**The lesson is sharper than "intervene on misses."** Every one of those misses
was a sentence my own prose had put in their mouth. The heron's bill is
described as *a spear held level*; they typed "grab the spear" and got "There is
no the spear here to take." The quay description says *Nobody is going to put it
out*; they typed "put the light out" and got nothing at all. I wrote the dare
and then refused to hear it. **Anything I name vividly enough to be reached for
has to be reachable by name.** That belongs in the validator eventually: a noun
that appears in a description or a monster line and matches no trigger in that
room is a miss waiting to happen.

**What I did, quickly.** A `quay-heron-hands` interaction, placed *after* the
two look-at-heron ones so examining still wins, catching grab/catch/sneak/
touch/pet/shoo/bill/spear/feather/heron/bird. It says the spear is attached, at
eye height, and that you will not get hold of it with your hands; it names
fighting as the only real way at it and declines to recommend it. The choice
stays theirs, which was the whole point of the heron. And the light-out
phrasings now reach `lamp-burning`, whose answer — *you could lift it down, you
are not going to* — was already right and just unreachable.

Validator caught three glob-shape holes, all fixed. Deployed, 8/8.

I did not speak to Lazer. The world speaks for me; that is what the edit was
for. Whether they now fight the bird is still their sentence to write.
